title: The summary for Thursday 19 November
text:
Good morning, it is Thursday 19 November: this is the GERICO summary.

In Shenzhen, China, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin spoke for about forty minutes on the sidelines of the APEC summit. This was reported by Ansa. The White House describes it as an informal conversation. What they discussed was not disclosed. A three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled for today. Expected topics include Iran, Ukraine, and nuclear weapons.

Regarding Iran, the Times of Israel writes, citing sources, that Trump is considering a new offensive, perhaps after the new year. Following the exchange of fire between the United States and Iran in the Gulf, one American aircraft carrier has left the area and two remain, writes Il Post.

In Ukraine, according to Reuters, Ukrainian attacks have reduced oil processing in Russia by 45%. The Crimean Bridge was hit again overnight and train traffic is suspended, says the Russian Ministry of Transport. The Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin today. Meanwhile, the European Commission is proposing a new loan of 45 billion euros for Ukraine.

In the world of technology, Anthropic has set the price of its public offering at 83 dollars per share. It has raised more than 81 billion dollars, the largest listing ever. The debut on the Nasdaq is today.

Let's move on to the markets. Yesterday, European stock exchanges closed lower. Milan lost 1.3%, at 50,000 points. Frankfurt fell 1.2%, London 1.3%, and Paris less than one percent. The spread between BTPs and Bunds was at 108 bp.

On commodities, WTI oil lost over 4%, at 82 dollars per barrel. Gold fell 2.6%, to 3,747 dollars per ounce. Bitcoin is at about 62,000 dollars, the lowest level in four months, writes Ansa.

On exchange rates, yesterday the euro-dollar lost 0.27%. The dollar-yen is around 159.50. Wall Street had closed sharply lower on Tuesday: the Dow Jones down 1.6%, the S&P 500 down 1%. Yesterday's closing is not yet available in the sources.

Among today's events, at 14:30 ECB President Christine Lagarde will speak. At the same time, the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index and weekly jobless claims will be released in the United States. In the morning, at 10:00, the International Court of Justice in The Hague will deliver its ruling on the Rohingya case against Myanmar.

The full news, with sources, is on GERICO. No investment advice.
